compensation_details: $3,000–$5,750 stipend plus free housing

eligibility.eligibility_text_raw: 2026 applications closed; cycles typically open in fall with winter deadlines

description: Umbrella of ~10-week, full-time summer biomedical research internships at the School of Medicine (2026: May 24–August 1) with stipends of $3,000–$5,750 and free housing. Open to current undergraduates at U.S. colleges; concurrent coursework or employment is prohibited.

title: Careers in Science and Medicine Summer Internship Program (CSM SIP) — Johns Hopkins School of Medicine
organization: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine
department: Department of Cell Biology / CSM Initiative
compensation_details: Minimum $3,000 stipend plus free housing

eligibility.eligibility_text_raw: Summer 2027 applications open fall 2026

description:
The undergraduate component of the Johns Hopkins Initiative for Careers in Science and Medicine: a ~10-week mentored summer research experience modeled on a first-year graduate lab rotation, with a minimum $3,000 stipend and free housing. Targets low-income (<200% federal poverty level), educationally under-resourced, and first-generation students interested in science, medicine, and public health careers. Includes professional development, networking, and a closing research presentation; some scholars continue into the Doctoral Development Program.

compensation_details: NSF REU stipend plus paid housing and travel allowance

title: Genomics and Society Mentorship Program (GSMP) — Johns Hopkins Berman Institute of Bioethics
compensation_details: $5,000 stipend

eligibility.eligibility_text_raw: Applications typically due February 1 for the summer cohort

description:
A 15-month hybrid program beginning with a 10-week summer internship ($5,000 stipend) researching the ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) of genomics, mentored by Berman Institute bioethics faculty. Trainees take foundational courses in the Berman Summer Institute, join weekly journal clubs and seminars, and continue mentored work through the academic year. Open to full-time college students who have completed at least one year; aims to broaden participation in ELSI research.

compensation_details: Stipend (two-summer training program)

description:
A two-summer, mentor-guided research-training experience at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health focused on aging research — Alzheimer's disease and related dementias — and on addressing health disparities. Builds research competencies and professional skills for undergraduates in MSTEM (medicine, science, technology, engineering, math) fields, especially students underrepresented in aging research.
